title: Finite and compatible completed local bases of the root tower
statement:
For any scheme on which l is invertible, the concrete finite root modules [def-pur-twist-sheaves] admit etale unit trivializations and have finite geometric stalks. The completed root module admits a pro-etale unit trivialization, and its ordinary finite scalar reductions are the prescribed finite root modules. There is no coefficient field or derived-completeness assertion.

theorem purTwistRootLocalModels (S : Scheme.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    [∀ x : S, Invertible (l : S.residueField x)] :
    (∀ n : ℕ,
      (∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (U : I → S.ProEt)
        (f : ∀ i : I, U i ⟶ ProEt.mk (𝟙 S)),
        Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ (ProEt.precoverage S).coverings _ ∧
        (∀ i : I, Etale (U i).hom) ∧
        ∀ i : I, Nonempty ((purTwistRootsModule S l n).over (U i) ≅
          (SheafOfModules.unit (purTwistRing S (purTwistFiniteRing S l n))).over (U i))) ∧
      (∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S),
        Finite ((proEtaleGeometricStalk (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) s
          (proEtaleRootsOfUnitySheaf S (l ^ (n + 1)))) : Type (u + 1)))) ∧
    ((∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (U : I → S.ProEt)
        (f : ∀ i : I, U i ⟶ ProEt.mk (𝟙 S)),
        Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ (ProEt.precoverage S).coverings _ ∧
        ∀ i : I, Nonempty ((purTwistZlModule S l).over (U i) ≅
          (SheafOfModules.unit (purTwistRing S (purTwistZlCompletion S l))).over (U i))) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, Nonempty
        (SheafOfModules.changeOfRingsOfUniverses.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u + 1}
          (purTwistZlProjection S l n)
          (purTwistZlModule S l) ≅ purTwistRootsModule S l n))

proof.text: Finite-level trivializations on the correct site. Work first over an affine open $T=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset S$, and put $N=\ell^r$. Apply lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line with $A=\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z$ and twist exponent $1$. The tensor with the coefficient ring is the identity (the maps $z\otimes a\mapsto z^a$ and $z\mapsto z\otimes1$ are inverse), so its conclusion is an etale cover trivializing the ordinary etale roots-of-unity sheaf. To transfer this particular sheaf, rather than assume an identification of sites, put $P=\operatorname{Spec}(B[X]/(X^N-1))$. On every $T$-scheme, maps to $P$ are precisely units $z$ with $z^N=1$, by the defining polynomial relation (the inverse of $z$ is $z^{N-1}$). Taking $g=1$ in lem-sbc-root-split-away-cover-etale makes its basic open all of $P$, so $P\to T$ is etale. Thus $P$ is an object of the etale site. In the explicit left-Kan-extension formula of def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, a representative $a\in h_P(U)$ at $(U,W\to U)$ maps to the composite $W\to U\xrightarrow a P$. Its inverse sends $b:W\to P$ to $\mathrm{id}_P$ at $(P,b)$. These are inverse: the arrow $(U,W\to U)\to(P,b)$ is $a$, and its restriction sends $\mathrm{id}_P$ to $a$. Consequently $\nu_T^{-1}h_P=h_P$ on the pro-etale site, after sheafification; the right side is the roots-of-unity sheaf in def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf. Apply clause 1 of the current statement of lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact with the finite discrete commutative ring $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z$: it identifies $\nu_T^{-1}\Lambda_{T_{\mathrm{et}}}$ with $\Lambda_{T_{\mathrm{proet}}}$ and the module inverse image with the underlying inverse image. For each etale trivializing member $U_i\to T$, repeat the preceding representative calculation with $W\to U_i$ and $P\times_TU_i$: a root over $W$ is exactly a $U_i$-map $W\to P\times_TU_i$. The etale isomorphism on $U_i$ and its inverse therefore pull back to inverse module morphisms on $(U_i)_{\mathrm{proet}}$, with the indicated constant coefficient ring. These are precisely the restrictions of the roots sheaf on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$, since both evaluate on $W$ as roots in $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)^\times$. Thus the same etale cover trivializes the pro-etale roots sheaf; no conclusion about integral twists or derived completeness is taken from this finite-coefficient comparison lemma. The power maps and scalar actions are unchanged because the displayed inverse is evaluation of the same root. Combining with the affine-open cover gives the first asserted rank-one local trivializations over $S$. No quasi-compactness or separation assumption on $S$ is used.

Choose compatible primitive roots on one covering. Start with the etale cover in step 1 for $r=1$, with its generator $\zeta_1$. Cover each member by affine objects $V$ weakly contractible for the full $S$-pro-etale site using lem-weil-pbc-proetale-affine-wcontractible-covering-family. This composite is a pro-etale covering of $S$. Fix such a $V$. Inductively, after choosing $\zeta_r\in\mu_{\ell^r}(V)$, apply its stated surjectivity of sections on $V$ to the epimorphism of step 2 to choose $\zeta_{r+1}$ with $\zeta_{r+1}^\ell=\zeta_r$. The base generator still trivializes $\mu_\ell|_V$. Each $\zeta_r$ generates $\mu_{\ell^r}|_V$: locally trivialize both finite sheaves of the composite power map to $\mu_\ell$, and refine until the image of the source generator and $\zeta_r$ have constant coefficients $b\in\mathbf Z/\ell$ and $a\in\mathbf Z/\ell^r$. This refinement exists by lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets (for the constant rings) followed by lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local applied to their underlying constant set presheaves; these are generic-site statements, not their etale-only counterparts. The epimorphism onto $\mu_\ell$ forces $b\neq0$ on every nonempty member: if $b=0$, the target constant section $1$ could not locally lift, as nonempty covering members have geometric points and the constant-sheaf stalk in lem-weil-proetale-constant-sheaf-stalk distinguishes $0$ and $1$. The equation $\zeta_r^{\ell^{r-1}}=\zeta_1$ now says $b(a\bmod\ell)$ is the unit coefficient of $\zeta_1$. Thus $a\bmod\ell\neq0$, so $a$ is a unit modulo $\ell^r$. Multiplication by its inverse proves that $a$ generates. The local inverse morphisms glue by the sheaf axiom. We obtain compatible isomorphisms $\theta_r:(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_V\xrightarrow{\sim}\mu_{\ell^r}|_V$, $a\mapsto\zeta_r^a$, with $\theta_r\circ\mathrm{red}=(u\mapsto u^\ell)\circ\theta_{r+1}$. Empty members may simply be discarded.

Take the inverse limit and identify its finite quotients. Write $R=\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,S}$ and $M=\varprojlim_r\mu_{\ell^r,S}$. Give $M$ its $R$-action coordinatewise: $(a_r)_r\cdot(z_r)_r=(z_r^{a_r})_r$. Compatibility follows from reduction of $a_{r+1}$ modulo $\ell^r$ and $z_{r+1}^\ell=z_r$; the module identities hold coordinatewise. By def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit, sections of both limits are compatible tuples. Restriction to $V$ is evaluation on the slice site, identified with $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ by lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization, and hence commutes with these sectionwise limits. Taking the compatible $\theta_r$ of step 3 gives the $R|_V$-linear isomorphism $R|_V\xrightarrow{\sim}M|_V$, with its $r$-th projection exactly $\theta_r\circ p_r$. Apply the quotient clause of lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence with $A=\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $I=(\ell)$. It is Noetherian because it is a DVR (each ideal is principal), and its quotient $A/I^r$ is $\mathbf Z/\ell^r$ by def-weil-l-adic-numbers. Thus $R/\ell^rR=(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_S$. On each $V$, the projection induces $M/\ell^rM\cong\mu_{\ell^r}$. These are the restrictions of the global canonical projection-induced map, so they glue to the global isomorphism. The tensor with a quotient ring is its quotient module: $m\otimes\bar a\mapsto\overline{am}$ and $\bar m\mapsto m\otimes1$ are inverse, first sectionwise and then after sheafification. Therefore $M\otimes_R(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_S\cong\mu_{\ell^r,S}$, compatibly with the power/reduction transitions.
